newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to scrap banks' foreign liabilities ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to scrap banks' foreign liabilities ceiling.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Thursday it was junking a ceiling on banks' foreign liabilities in its drive to liberalise the financial markets and comply with international practices.
"The central bank has decided to scrap rules on foreign liabilities ceiling starting immediately to further liberalise its foreign exchange market," the bank said in a statement.
The central bank said the move to eliminate the ceiling could expand the scale of banks' foreign currency loan business and allow banks to be more flexibile with their funds.
The central bank may request unspecified reserves from banks' foreign liabilities outstanding to ensure stability in the financial market, it said.
Before the liberalisation, the central bank set a ceiling on banks' total foreign liabilities outstanding at US$30.2 billion.
As of May 21, both local and foreign banks' combined foreign liabilities outstanding totalled US$13.3 billion.
